problem: "60 Hz means 60 passes per second" can be misread as 60 scan lines per second, since a 'pass' is not a defined term.
fix: "60 Hz means the whole screen is redrawn 60 times each second, that is, 60 frames per second."

problem: "It halves the signal rate" does not say what it is halved compared with, and 'combing' is really a de-interlacing artefact; the artefact of interlacing itself on motion is edge jaggedness (interline twitter).
fix: "Compared with progressive scan at the same frame rate, interlacing halves the bandwidth the signal needs. The cost is jagged edges on moving objects and fine horizontal detail, because each field carries only half the lines."

problem: Only vertical retrace is named. The beam also has to fly back from the end of each scan line to the start of the next, and students meet this 'horizontal retrace' (and blanking) in exam questions.
fix: Add after the vertical retrace sentence: "The short return from the end of one scan line to the start of the next is horizontal retrace. The beam is switched off during both retraces; this off time is blanking."

problem: 'Frame size' is used loosely for what the formula actually gives: the size of the frame buffer in bytes, not the size of the frame in pixels.
fix: "Frame buffer size in bytes = image width in pixels × image height in pixels × bytes per pixel."
